definitions.explanation: A plant of the Brassica family grown for its oil-rich seeds and as a green vegetable. Its bright yellow flowers are an iconic sight of spring in Japan.

examples.japanese: {油菜|あぶらな}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{咲|さ}いている→咲く：08150_saku⟧。
⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{畑|はたけ}→畑：00842_hatake⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{油菜|あぶらな}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{黄色|きいろ}→黄色：02870_kiiro⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧。
examples.english: When spring comes, the fields are dyed yellow with rapeseed.

examples.japanese: {油菜|あぶらな}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{食用|しょくよう}→食用：25328_shokuyou⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{栽培|さいばい}→栽培：13108_saibai⟧⟦され→する：00392_suru⟧、おひたしや⟦{炒|いた}め{物|もの}→炒め物：08537_itamemono⟧にして⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: Rapeseed is also grown as a food crop and eaten as boiled greens or in stir-fries.

notes:
Literally 'oil vegetable' — named because its seeds are pressed to produce cooking oil ({菜種油|なたねあぶら}). The plant is also known as ⟦{菜|な}の{花|はな}→菜の花：14042_nanohana⟧ (canola flower), especially when referring to the flowers or the plant as a spring symbol.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Fields of brilliant yellow {油菜|あぶらな} flowers are a beloved spring sight in Japan. ⟦{菜|な}の{花|はな}→菜の花：14042_nanohana⟧ is a seasonal word (⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧) for spring in haiku. The plant is also eaten as a vegetable — the young shoots and flower buds are a spring delicacy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {油菜|あぶらな}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧ — rapeseed flower
- ⟦{菜種|なたね}→菜種：24601_natane⟧⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧ — rapeseed oil, canola oil
- {油菜|あぶらな}{畑|ばたけ} — rapeseed field

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{菜|な}の{花|はな}→菜の花：14042_nanohana⟧ — canola flower; the popular name for the flowers and the edible shoots
- ⟦{菜種|なたね}→菜種：24601_natane⟧ — rapeseed; refers specifically to the seeds
- ⟦{白菜|はくさい}→白菜：13606_hakusai⟧ — Chinese cabbage; a related Brassica vegetable
